what.text: This page follows refugees from Myanmar in all host countries combined.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 1524378 refugees from Myanmar, and Bangladesh hosts the largest share, 77.3%.
Malaysia, Thailand and India are the next largest hosts.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Myanmar in several periods since 1967; from 2021 to 2025 the opposing groups include the NUG, PSLF, CNF and PNLO, at war level from 2022.
In the main displacement years it also records armed conflict over Arakan territory, with ARSA and ULA from 2016 to 2020 and ULA from 2022 to 2025.
Conflicts over Kachin, Karen and Karenni territory are recorded from 2021 to 2025, with the KIO, the KNU and the KNPP.

when.text: UNHCR's figure rose from 5700 in 1972 to 1524378 in 2025, its highest.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2017 to 2025, after a big change between 2016 and 2017.
Returns to Myanmar were highest in 1979 in UNHCR's returns data.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees; asylum seekers from Myanmar are counted in a separate series.
People displaced inside Myanmar are counted separately by UNHCR and by IDMC, and their figures are never added.
The sources don't say which routes people took.
